modern_card.name: Green Baboon, Defender of the Forest

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (LCYW-EN165, Legendary Collection 3: Yugi's World Mega Pack)

transitions.historical_text: When a Beast-Type monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard, you can pay 1000 Life Points to Special Summon this card from your hand or the Graveyard.
transitions.modern_text: If this card is in your hand or Graveyard when a face-up Beast-Type monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard (except during the Damage Step): You can pay 1000 Life Points; Special Summon this card.
transitions.summary: Wording only, on Konami's lists and the period card rulings (round 036). (a) Damage Step: Konami's errata lists (compiled 2009-07-30, 2010-01-05, 2010-11-05) say "You cannot activate the effect of this card during the Damage Step", which replaced the earlier card FAQ entry that allowed it, and the rulebook's Damage Step rule agrees. (b) Face-up: the UDE Netrep (answer 2007-09-28) says of a Beast destroyed face-down "You cannot activate the effect of "Green Baboon, Defender of the Forest" in this case", and the card FAQ (Konami-hosted 2008-12-15) says the effect "can be activated after a Beast-Type monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard, if that monster was face-up" and "You cannot activate this effect when a face-down Beast-Type monster you control is destroyed by a card effect." Under the owner's decision of 2026-09-29 (docs/state.md, "Period rulings") a UDE-era card ruling counts at Edison and Tengu unless a later Konami document replaced it. Konami's lists, which replaced the FAQ on the Damage Step, say nothing on face-up. So the era card and the errata'd card match on both points. Konami's lists also say that when several copies are available only 1 may be Special Summoned; one two-copy scenario was run (Dark Hole, two copies in hand) and the modern card Special Summoned one, so no difference is established.

implementation_metadata.reason: Round 036: the generated card 600000006 (rounds 031 and 035) was removed and its number retired. On Konami's lists (Damage Step) and the UDE/Konami card rulings counted under the owner's decision of 2026-09-29 (face-up), the era card behaves as the modern card, so the modern implementation is used; no script or engine test is needed for it.

review.notes:
The packet's single upstream entry, 511001661 "Green Baboon, Defender of the Forest (Manga)" in cards-unofficial.cdb, is a DIFFERENT card, not a historical version of 46668237: it triggers off Insect/Beast/Plant/Beast-Warrior monsters on either side of the field and its text matches the lineage at only ratio 0.7277. It cannot serve as a baseline implementation, so this card remains a genuine gap. Its script is still useful corroboration: the older-style trigger is scripted with EVENT_DESTROYED plus EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP+EFFECT_FLAG_DELAY, while the modern Green Baboon script (the '-' side of the diff) uses EVENT_TO_GRAVE with no damage-step property - the script-level counterpart of the errata's added "(except during the Damage Step)". Era text: v0 (JUMP-EN014, 2007-07-15) is in force for Edison (2010-04-24); the card postdates GOAT. Trailing cosmetic revision v1 -> v2 (SBCB-EN053, 2020-11-26: GY wording, "Beast monster", location clause moved) is not recorded as a change; cards.cdb matches v2 exactly. Green Baboon is not on the EdisonFormat.com Functional Errata list.

Round 035 (2026-09-29) evidence, added and nothing replaced. (a) The Damage Step half of the summary above is contradicted at both snapshots by Konami's own lists: "Green Baboon, Defender of the Forest ... You cannot activate the effect of this card during the Damage Step." (Current Card Errata Lists compiled 2009-07-30, 2010-01-05 and 2010-11-05; Konami's Gameplay page called the 2010-01-05 list "Current Errata" on 2010-03-22 and the 2010-11-05 list on 2011-09-18), and by Konami's rulebook Damage Step rule (Versions 7.0 to 8.0). The earlier UDE/Konami card FAQ said the opposite ("can be activated during the Damage Step", capture 2008-12-15); the later Konami list overrides it. The generated script now excludes the Damage Step. (b) The face-up half: the UDE Netrep (answer 2007-09-28) and the card FAQ (2008-12-15) say a face-down Beast destroyed does not trigger it; Konami's lists are silent on face-up. Whether that ruling held at the snapshots is not shown, so the script keeps the printed-text reading (no face-up requirement) and the question is on the owner's list. (c) Konami's lists also say that when several copies are available only 1 may be Special Summoned; in the one two-copy scenario run (Dark Hole, two copies in hand) the modern and the generated script each Special Summoned one. Evidence: docs/research/period-rulings-generated-scripts.md, section 6.5.

Round 036 (2026-09-29) correction. Round 035 corrected the Damage Step half and kept the face-up half for the owner. The owner then decided on 2026-09-29 (docs/state.md, "Period rulings") that a UDE-era card ruling counts at Edison and Tengu unless a later Konami document replaced it. The face-up rulings were re-read at their sources: the UDE Judge List thread (Netrep answer of 2007-09-28: "1) You cannot activate the effect of "Green Baboon, Defender of the Forest" in this case." for a Beast destroyed while face-down by Torrential Tribute or Shield Crash) and the card FAQ (Konami-hosted 2008-12-15, page F-H: "This effect can be activated after a Beast-Type monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard, if that monster was face-up and "Green Baboon, Defender of the Forest" was in your hand or Graveyard when it was destroyed." and "You cannot activate this effect when a face-down Beast-Type monster you control is destroyed by a card effect."). Konami's errata lists say nothing on face-up either way, so nothing later replaces the rulings on that point. The generated script differed from Project Ignis's official/c46668237.lua only in dropping the face-up filter, so with the ruling applied nothing else differs from the modern card. Evidence and its limits: docs/research/period-rulings-generated-scripts.md, section 6.5 and the round-036 section. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Functional erratum on two points. The era text triggers off "a Beast-Type monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard" with no position requirement and no Damage Step exclusion; the errata'd text requires the destroyed Beast to have been face-up and adds "(except during the Damage Step)". So the era card can pay 1000 LP and Special Summon itself off a face-down Beast being destroyed, and can do so inside the Damage Step when a Beast is destroyed by battle - the exact window a period Beast deck uses. Both restrictions are baked into the modern implementation, whose trigger is EVENT_TO_GRAVE with a POS_FACEUP previous-position filter and no EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP property." Superseded implementation note, kept verbatim: "Round 031: implemented by a project-authored script under the custom-script strategy (data/custom-cards/c600000006.json; passcode 600000006). Previously recorded as a known gap with gap_reason "Project Ignis ships no historical implementation of this card; reproducing the era behaviour needs a custom script and a reserved passcode" (gap_sources ignis-babelcdb, yugipedia-card-errata). Status is partial, not complete: the custom card's not_reproduced list names what the script does not establish. Round 035 (2026-09-29): the script no longer allows the Damage Step (Konami's errata lists and rulebook forbid it); only the face-up difference remains." Superseded gap statement, kept verbatim: "In an Edison snapshot EDOPro refuses the Damage Step Green Baboon revival after a Beast is destroyed by battle, and refuses it entirely when the destroyed Beast was face-down, so a period Beast deck loses plays that its 2007-2010 text allows. Round 035 (2026-09-29): the Damage Step half of this statement is withdrawn; Konami's period lists forbid the Damage Step activation, so the modern card is period-correct there. The face-down half stands on the printed text alone; a UDE ruling says otherwise and is on the owner's list."
